editorial_contributions.text: A \(2\)-coloring of the diagonals (including sides) of a regular convex \(n\)-gon is a circulant coloring of \(K_n\) if all diagonals of the same length have the same color. Corresponding to such colorings are two circulant Ramsey numbers \(RC_1(G,H)\) and \(RC_2(G,H)\) such that for all \(n < RC_1(G,H)\) a circulant coloring without a monochromatic \(G\) or \(H\) exists and for all \(n \geq RC_2\) no such coloring exists. The Ramsey numbers \(RC_1\) and \(RC_2\) are determined for all paths, cycles, graphs on at most five vertices, and for some small complete graphs. As a consequence of the latter results, new lower bounds \(R(K_4,K_{10}) \geq 92\) and \(R(K_5,K_8) \geq 101\) for classical Ramsey numbers are obtained.

Summary: We study the perfect colorings of infinite circulant graphs whose set of distances constitutes the segment of naturals \([1, n]\). We give a complete description of the perfect colorings of these graphs with two colors and list all their admissible parameters.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: A coloring of the vertex set in a graph is called perfect if all its identically colored vertices have identical multisets of colors of their neighbors. Refer as the infinite circulant graph with continuous set of \(n\) distances to the Cayley graph of the group \(\mathbb Z\) with generator set \(\{1,2,\dots, n\}\). We obtain a description of all perfect colorings with an arbitrary number of colors of this graph with distances 1 and 2. In [\textit{O. G. Parshina}, Diskretn. Anal. Issled. Oper. 21, No. 2, 76--83 (2014; Zbl 1324.05064); translation in J. Appl. Ind. Math. 8, No. 3, 357--361 (2014)], there was made a conjecture characterizing perfect colorings for the infinite circulant graphs with a continuous set of \(n\) distances. The obtained result confirms the conjecture for \(n=2\). The problem is still open in the case of \(n>2\).

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Total coloring of a graph is a variety of proper colorings in which no two adjacent vertices, edges incident on the same vertex, or an edge and its incident vertices receive the same color. The total chromatic number is the minimum number of colors required in any total coloring of a graph. The neighbor-sum distinguishing and equitable total chromatic numbers are generalizations of the total chromatic number. The computation of all three numbers is shown to be NP-hard. The circulant graphs are regular graphs with varying applications within and outside graph theory. They are the easiest examples of regular graphs that come to mind. They can be seen as the Cayley graphs on cyclic groups. In this paper, we have obtained better bounds for the total chromatic and equitable and neighborsum distinguishing total chromatic numbers of some classes of the circulant graphs.

editorial_contributions.text:
Summary: A distance graph (resp. circulant graph) is a graph obtained from the path (resp. the cycle) of order \(n\) by adding chordal edges between any pair of vertices at distance \(d\in D\), with \(D \subset \mathbb Z_{n}\). The chromatic sum of a graph is the smallest sum of colors among all proper colorings of this graph. This paper studies the chromatic sum for some classes of distance graphs and circulant graphs depending on the value of \(D\).

For the entire collection see [Zbl 1109.05013].

source.source: Discrete Math. Algorithms Appl. 11, No. 1, Article ID 1950005, 10 p. (2019).

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Given a digraph $D$ with no loops, the \textit{dicoloring graph} of $D$, denoted by $\mathcal{D}_k(D)$, is the graph whose vertices are the acyclic $k$-colorings of $D$ and two colorings are adjacent in $\mathcal{D}_k(D)$ if they differ in color on exactly one vertex. In this paper, we prove that there is no expression $ϕ(\vecχ)$ in terms of the dichromatic number $\vecχ$, such that the graph $\mathcal{D}_k(D)$ is connected for all graphs $D$ and integers $k\geq ϕ(\vecχ)$. We give conditions for the dicoloring graph of two infinite families of circulant tournaments to be connected, and we provide upper bounds for its diameter. In particular, for the Payley tournament $\vec{C}_{7}(1,2,4)$, also known as $ST_7$, we prove that $\mathcal{D}_k(\vec{C}_{7}(1,2,4))$ is connected and has diameter 8, for each $k\geq 3$.

title.title: Redicoloring some classes of circulant tournaments
